reference: Frozen original GGML graph constructors and CPU executor, one CPU thread. No Rust execution or expected-value substitution.
notes: TOP_K preserves the source's final swap of the first two selected indices.
ARGSORT and TOP_K ties are platform STL behavior. Windows and GNU fixtures are captured independently, never relabeled across platforms.
SET_ROWS duplicate indices use the source's one-thread last-row overwrite semantics; F16-to-F16 copies raw payload bytes.
ACC overlapping rows read the original base, not earlier writes.
CPU from_float availability is separately checked against the original runtime trait table; generic stored-model quantizers are not substituted for missing CPU converters.
CAST Q8_1/Q8_K to F32 is absent in the source CPU trait table and excluded; their activation encoders and SET_ROWS destinations are independently captured.

GNU x86_64 defines __SSE2__ even when GGML_SSE42 is OFF; MSVC /arch:SSE4.2 does not. The source F32 dot/sum use scalar F64 accumulation in both builds, but source SiLU/softmax separately use SSE2 exponential paths on GNU. The indexing corpus does not execute those activation operators.

Windows and GNU build options are recorded exactly, not described as identical. Windows enables SSE42/BMI2/OpenMP/LLAMAFILE in its CMake cache; GNU disables them. Both graphs execute with one CPU thread.
MSVC sorting policy targets STL 14.51.36231, built with compiler 19.51.36260.0; GNU sorting policy targets GNU 11.4.0. Equal-key ordering is not a portable C++ guarantee.
NaN sort keys are excluded: the source comparator does not establish a strict weak ordering for arbitrary NaN-containing rows. Rust explicitly rejects that undefined comparator domain.
Integer conversions reject nonfinite or out-of-range inputs instead of reproducing C float-to-integer undefined behavior.
All 890 outputs compare exact bytes, including packed encoder bytes, signed zero and preserved NaN payloads. The separate prior transcendental comparison criteria are not used by this corpus.
